demo.title: Two models, one sample task
demo.notice: Demonstration — synthetic sample data, not Sakshi's project results
demo.provenance: Hand-authored synthetic teaching fixture for this portfolio UI. No dataset was collected and no model was trained; these are not Sakshi’s project results.
demo.description: Imagine two unnamed models sorting items into Class 0 or Class 1. Compare their illustrative scores, follow their loss over six passes through training, and inspect their sample prediction counts. Neither model represents a portfolio project.
demo.accuracyExplanation: Accuracy is the share of predictions that match the known class. The unit is percent (%); higher means more correct predictions on that set. Training uses examples seen during fitting; validation uses held-out examples. These invented validation counts contain 100 items per model, with 50 in each class. Training sample size is not represented. Accuracy alone does not describe every kind of error.
demo.lossExplanation: Binary cross-entropy loss describes how far predicted probabilities are from the known classes. It is a unitless score; lower is better on the same task and set. An epoch is one pass through the training examples. These six hand-authored points illustrate curves only; they are not calculated from the prediction-count tables. A training curve alone cannot establish performance on unseen data.
demo.matrixExplanation: A confusion matrix counts correct and incorrect predictions. Rows are the known class; columns are the predicted class. Matching row/column classes are correct predictions. Each synthetic table has 100 validation items. These counts explain the sample validation accuracy; they do not establish real model quality.
